candidates.reason: TX ring descriptor single-fetch is correct: '*desc = READ_ONCE(ring->desc[idx]);' copies the whole struct xdp_desc into the caller's kernel stack copy, then xskq_validate_desc (xsk_queue.h:186-201) validates that same local copy via xskq_is_valid_desc (xsk_queue.h:172-184: addr < q->size and (addr+len)&chunk_mask == addr&chunk_mask). Both fetches of the same memory occur exactly once; every downstream consumer uses the local copy, so no check-then-use double fetch exists on the TX ring.

FILL ring address single-fetch is correct: '*addr = READ_ONCE(ring->desc[idx]) & q->chunk_mask;' reads the user-mapped u64 once, masks it, and validates the resulting local value with xskq_is_valid_addr (xsk_queue.h:80-88: addr >= q->size rejected). Callers __xsk_rcv (xsk.c:63-69) and xsk_generic_rcv (xsk.c:133-139) add headroom to and use only the local 'addr'; neither re-reads the ring entry.

xsk_generic_xmit copy-mode TX path (xsk.c:233-272) validates once via xskq_peek_desc into local 'struct xdp_desc desc' and then uses only locals: len = desc.len (line 249), addr = desc.addr (line 257), buffer = xdp_umem_get_data(umem, addr), skb_store_bits(skb, 0, buffer, len). No second fetch from the user-mapped ring between the validation inside xskq_validate_desc and the skb copy; the use equals the validated value.

xsk_umem_consume_tx (xsk.c:173-197), the zerocopy driver TX entry, copies the descriptor once into a local struct via xskq_peek_desc (validated), then derives cq produce address (line 183), dma = xdp_umem_get_dma(umem, desc.addr) (line 186) and *len = desc.len (line 187) all from the same validated local copy. No re-read of the shared ring.

Ring count indices are also single-fetch cached: xskq_nb_avail (xsk_queue.h:53-64) does q->prod_tail = READ_ONCE(q->ring->producer) once and computes entries from the cached kernel-side q->prod_tail/cons_tail; xskq_nb_free (xsk_queue.h:66-76) likewise caches READ_ONCE(q->ring->consumer) into q->cons_tail. The cached values, not re-fetched shared memory, gate xskq_nb_free/xskq_reserve_addr space checks used by produce paths, so the checked and used count cannot diverge.

i40e_xmit_zc (i40e_xsk.c:~738-782) consumes TX descriptors only through xsk_umem_consume_tx(umem, &dma, &len), whose dma/len outputs come from the validated local desc copy (xsk.c:173-197); the driver then uses those locals for dma_sync_single_for_device, tx_bi->bytecount and the hardware descriptor. No direct access to the user-mapped TX ring occurs in the driver.

ixgbe_xmit_zc (ixgbe_xsk.c:628-674) mirrors i40e: descriptors arrive only via xsk_umem_consume_tx into local dma/len, which feed dma_sync_single_for_device, cmd_type_len and olinfo_status. No second fetch from shared memory. i40e/ixgbe are the only in-tree consumers of the xsk_umem_*/xdp_umem_* TX APIs found in s02 (grep over drivers/, net/, include/).

Seed-function analogue does not exist in s02: tree-wide grep of s02 for 'xsk_skb_metadata', 'xsk_tx_metadata', 'XDP_TXMD', 'tx_metadata_len' and 'csum' over net/xdp/, include/net/xdp_sock.h and include/uapi/linux/if_xdp.h returns zero matches (rc=1). The s02 tree is an early AF_XDP vintage (struct xdp_umem API, no buff pool, no TX metadata) that predates commit 48eb03dd2630 which introduced the seed's vulnerable feature, so the direct structural analogue is absent rather than fixed. Listed as unresolved because absence is verified only by identifier and feature grep, not by line-by-line reading of every function.

limitations: s02's AF_XDP implementation predates XDP TX-metadata support (no xsk_tx_metadata struct, XDP_TXMD flags, or csum fields anywhere in its net/xdp and xdp_sock headers), so the seed's exact feature is not present in this snapshot; the audit therefore covered the descriptor and fill-ring data paths that do exist.

Candidate audit was bounded to s02's net/xdp core (xsk.c, xsk_queue.c/h, xdp_umem.c/h, include/net/xdp_sock.h) plus the two in-tree drivers (i40e, ixgbe) that consume the exported xsk_umem_*/xdp_umem_* API; other drivers in s02 do not implement ndo_xsk_async_xmit consumers of these symbols per tree-wide grep.

The xdp_desc.options field is declared in s02's uapi (include/uapi/linux/if_xdp.h:70-74) but is never read by any kernel consumer in s02, so no check/use pair exists for it; this was established by grep of all desc-field accesses, not by exhaustive per-driver reading.
Negative result is about the check-then-use double-fetch invariant only; other bug classes (e.g. producer/consumer race windows, memory ordering) in the same ring code were not audited.
